translation: The qigu (岐骨) is the place where the ends of the two fugua bones (鳧骨) meet, and below it is the jiuwei bone (鳩尾骨). It is near the heart sovereign internally, and is most forbidden to be struck. Whether struck by a fall or knocked by a horse, the blood will necessarily become congested and stagnant, and there will be much pain. In mild cases it is only above the diaphragm; in severe cases it must enter the heart viscus, causing clouded spirit and closed eyes, unconsciousness, clenched teeth and locked jaw, panting with phlegm and flaring nostrils; if it lasts long without waking, and upon waking the spirit is confused, this is blood stasis that has hardened and does not move, and it is difficult to restore life. If the spirit is not confused, and there is only unceasing stasis pain, a full chest and hurried breathing, silence without speaking, and upon waking one can still take a little food and drink, one should in the morning take Jiajian Suzi Taoren Tang (Modified Perilla-Seed and Peach-Kernel Decoction, 加減蘇子桃仁湯) with Zhiqiao (bitter orange) added, in the evening take Shuxue Wan (Blood-Dispersing Pill, 疏血丸), externally apply Wanling Gao (Myriad-Efficacy Plaster, 萬靈膏), and then iron on Dingtong San (Pain-Relieving Powder, 定痛散) stir-fried hot, and it may then be cured.
